# Results — Study 415 (Triple Top & Bottom)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **three taps
at one level mark an exhausted trend; buy the confirmed triple-bottom breakout (and short the
triple-top breakdown)** — tested with an **objective, mechanical** detector on daily OHLC. Chart
figures are partly subjective, so we test the closest rules-based definition (three swing pivots
within a tolerance of one level, genuine bounces between them, then a confirmed neckline break)
and say so. For each confirmed breakout we measure the forward **5 / 10 / 20 / 40-day** return in
the trade's intended direction, **net of each name's own base rate**, with a 1-day entry lag.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **auto-adjusted** (split + dividend) OHLC — SPY + 29 long-listed US large-caps (public, no key) |
| As-of | **2026-05-31** (last bar **2026-05-29**; no partial month in the stamped run) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**21.4** years; **5,385** daily bars) |
| Panel | **30** names · fingerprint **`62992380d9e9`** |
| Detector | swing window 5; three taps within **4%** of the level; bounces ≥ **5%**; figure span 25–180 bars; breakout = first close through the neckline (buffer 0); non-overlapping |
| Breakouts | **356** confirmed triple-**bottoms** (SPY: 5) · **211** triple-**tops** (myth-check, SPY: 3) |
| Timing / costs | enter the close **1 day after** the breakout (no look-ahead); hold 5/10/20/40 days; **5 bps** one-way × 2 legs |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The basket is 30 names *still trading* in 2026. A
> fixed surviving-names panel cannot include names that delisted after a failed pattern, which
> tilts post-breakout forward returns mildly **up** — i.e. *for* the bullish triple-bottom read
> (and *against* the bearish triple-top short). The effect we report is, if anything, generous to
> the figure — and it still fails.

## The signal — triple-bottom (bullish, long) forward edge, EXCESS over base rate

The excess pools every confirmed breakout across the basket, subtracting each name's own
unconditional mean forward return (the base rate) so the test is "does the figure beat
buy-and-hold *for that name*", not "is the market up". *t* is one-sample; HAC *t* is Newey-West;
the placebo *p* is the share of **5,000 random-date entries** on the same tape whose pooled excess
**beats** the observed one.

| horizon | n | excess | raw | win-rate | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 356 | **+0.335%** | +0.644% | 56% | +1.75 | +1.82 | 0.369 | +0.235% |
| 10-day | 355 | +0.207% | +0.816% | 53% | +0.72 | +0.77 | 0.443 | +0.107% |
| 20-day | 354 | +0.389% | +1.600% | 55% | +0.79 | +0.86 | 0.421 | +0.289% |
| 40-day | 350 | **−0.689%** | +1.687% | 48% | −1.22 | −1.32 | 0.598 | −0.789% |

Read it carefully. The best excess anywhere is **+0.34% at 5 days** — and it sits at *t* = **1.75**
(HAC **1.82**), *under* the desk's **t ≥ 2** bar, with a placebo it cannot beat (random dates
match it ~37% of the time). The edge **decays** with horizon and turns **negative** by 40 days
(**−0.69%**, *t* = −1.22) — exactly the multi-week hold the lore tells you to ride. The raw column
is positive throughout only because the names drift up; once you net out that drift there is
nothing left.

## Robustness — the tiny edge is a tolerance artefact

If the figure were real, demanding a *cleaner* shape (tighter level tolerance, bigger bounces)
should *sharpen* it. It doesn't — the excess wanders around zero and the *t* never clears 2.

| level tol | min bounce | n | excess (5-day) | *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 3% | 7% | 126 | +0.322% | 0.87 | 0.424 |
| **4%** | **5%** | **356** | **+0.335%** | **1.75** | **0.367** |
| 6% | 4% | 641 | +0.018% | 0.13 | 0.492 |

The loosest setting (n = 641) collapses to **+0.02%** at *t* = 0.13. There is no strictness at
which "three failures at one level" becomes a signal.

## Myth check — the bearish triple top LOSES (no symmetric reversal)

A genuine reversal figure must work on **both** sides. We run the identical machinery on the
**triple top** (three peaks, confirmed break *below* the neckline) as a **short**, measuring the
short's excess over a short's base rate.

| horizon | n | short excess | raw | win-rate | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 211 | −0.050% | −0.360% | 54% | −0.15 | 0.510 |
| 10-day | 211 | −0.590% | −1.202% | 48% | −1.18 | 0.626 |
| 20-day | 210 | **−1.376%** | −2.598% | 43% | −2.04 | 0.701 |
| 40-day | 210 | **−1.941%** | −4.336% | 46% | −2.12 | 0.703 |

The triple-top short is **net-negative** and grows more negative with horizon (the negative *t* at
20–40d means it reliably *loses*, against the believer's direction). The names keep drifting **up**
through the "bearish" figure. This asymmetry is the diagnosis: the figure is **not** reading
exhaustion at a level — the bullish side only looked alive because it borrows the market's
up-drift, and the bearish side, which fights it, drowns.

## SPY-only — does the figure beat SPY buy-and-hold? (the README hook)

| horizon | n | excess | raw | *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 5 | +0.161% | +0.398% | 0.92 | 0.457 |
| 10-day | 5 | −0.089% | +0.381% | −0.11 | 0.559 |
| 20-day | 5 | +0.281% | +1.218% | 0.15 | 0.475 |
| 40-day | 5 | +0.699% | +2.546% | 0.46 | 0.434 |

On the index itself the detector fires only **5** times in 21 years — far too few to say anything,
and every *t* is near zero. The "buy the SPY triple bottom" recipe is a non-event.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic panel with *planted* triple bottoms, the same-tape placebo behaves exactly as
it must. Note the naive *t* is **negative** at edge 0 — the figure's geometry mechanically leaves
the breakout price near the neckline, so a raw *t* can be fooled either way; **the placebo, not the
raw t, is the arbiter**, and it correctly refuses the null.

| planted edge | planted | detected | n | excess (20-day) | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 160 | 218 | 218 | −1.64% | −5.06 | **0.828** | 38% |
| **+0.20** (large planted drift) | 160 | 209 | 209 | **+5.02%** | **+10.19** | **0.016** | 77% |

With **no** planted drift the placebo is **not beaten** (p = 0.83 — no false positive); a large
planted drift lights up at p = 0.016, *t* = +10, win 77%. The harness can clearly bank a real
edge — so the real-tape placebo *p* ≈ 0.37 is a genuine **nothing**, not a power failure.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The triple-bottom breakout excess peaks at **+0.34% at 5 days (t = 1.75, HAC
  t = 1.82, placebo p = 0.369)**, decays to **−0.69% at 40 days**, never clears the **t ≥ 2** bar
  at any horizon, and evaporates under the strictness sweep. Indistinguishable from noise once the
  tape's up-drift is netted out — and survivorship tilts *for* the figure, so this is generous.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of 5 bps/leg the 5-day excess is **+0.24%** (inside the placebo
  cloud) and the recommended 40-day hold is **−0.79%**. No deployable edge, nothing to scale.
- **"Reliable reversal"? — BUSTED.** The bearish **triple top** short is **net-negative**
  (−1.38% at 20d, −1.94% at 40d): the figure does not reverse symmetrically. The bullish side
  merely rides market drift; the bearish side fights it and loses. "Three failures at one level"
  is a shape the eye finds, not a force the tape obeys.
